messages.author: d3aaa07872b9962c
messages.subject: Linetypes
parts:
Is there a way to use other linetypes than the six built-in ones? Can
I (easily) implement my own linetypes? I would specifically be
interested in solid double lines (=====) and solid ladder-lines
(--|--|--|-- and ==|==|==|==). These would be used for plotting on a
map.

-- Osmo

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Linetypes
parts:
Hi,

It's easy to use custom linetypes but only in terms of spacing
specification, I believe (as in the rest of R graphics). See this
example,


library(maps)
states = map_data("state")
statenames = unique(states$region)
states <- subset(states, region %in% statenames[sample(1:length(statenames),5)])

ltys = c("22", "44", "13", "1343", "73", "2262", "12223242", "F282",
"F4448444", "224282F2", "F1")


qplot(long, lat, data = states, group = group,
linetype = factor(region), geom="path") +
scale_linetype_manual(values = ltys[1:5])

Making double lines and ladder-lines as you call them should be doable
if you superpose different geoms on top of each other, but it's
probably hard to automate. Try this for instance,


qplot(long, lat, data = states, group = group, geom="path",
linetype=I("solid"), size=I(2)) +
geom_path(size=1, colour="grey95") # match the background colour

HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Linetypes
parts:
> Daft question, but how would you convert line types into hex? Would
> would be the value for a solid line?
>
> Colin

I don't think there is an hex value for a solid (or blank for that
matter) line, but you can use "solid"

ltys = c("solid", "dashed", "51","15","11","FFAA")
grid.segments(rep(0,6),seq(0.2,0.8,len=6),rep(1,6),seq(0.2,0.8,len=6),gp=gpar(lty=ltys))

for the hex specification, you need an odd number of digits, and 0
isn't allowed as a length.

HTH,

baptiste
